task_groups.title: Implement Run method and GitError handling

subtasks.title: Implement the Run core execution method
details: Implement `func (r *GitRunner) Run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (string, error)` in `internal/gitcmd/gitcmd.go`
Create `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)` with `cmd.Dir = r.workDir` and `cmd.Env = r.env`
Capture stdout and stderr into separate `bytes.Buffer` instances
On success (exit code 0), return `strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil`
On failure, extract exit code via `*exec.ExitError` and return `nil, &GitError{Args: args, ExitCode: exitCode, Stderr: strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())}`
Handle context cancellation: if `ctx.Err() != nil` after command failure, still return `*GitError` with the exit code (or -1 if unavailable)

subtasks.title: Implement runWithExitCode helper for exit-code-aware methods
details: Implement an unexported `runWithExitCode(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (stdout string, exitCode int, stderr string, err error)` helper
This helper returns the raw exit code alongside stdout/stderr without wrapping in `*GitError`, enabling callers like `LsRemote` to perform exit-code discrimination
Use `errors.As(err, &exitErr)` with `*exec.ExitError` to extract the exit code
Return exit code -1 if the error is not an `*exec.ExitError` (e.g. binary not found)
Ensure all stdout/stderr strings are trimmed before return

subtasks.title: Implement RevParse and UpdateRef convenience methods
details: Implement `func (r *GitRunner) RevParse(ctx context.Context, ref string) (string, error)` calling `r.Run(ctx, "rev-parse", ref)`
Implement `func (r *GitRunner) UpdateRef(ctx context.Context, ref, sha string) error` calling `r.Run(ctx, "update-ref", ref, sha)` and discarding stdout
Both methods propagate `*GitError` from `Run` unchanged
Add godoc comments describing the git subcommand each method invokes

subtasks.title: Implement CONFLICT line parser for merge-tree output
details: Create `internal/gitcmd/conflict.go` with an unexported `parseConflictFiles(stdout string) []string` function
Scan stdout line-by-line using `strings.Split(stdout, "\n")`
Identify lines starting with `CONFLICT` prefix
Extract file path from each CONFLICT line — document the chosen parsing rule (regex, prefix strip, or delimiter split) in a code comment alongside a representative sample line from git 2.38+
Representative sample: `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in path/to/file.go` — extract `path/to/file.go` after the last `: ` delimiter
Return deduplicated slice of file paths; return empty slice (not nil) if no CONFLICT lines found

subtasks.title: Implement MergeTree method
details: Implement `func (r *GitRunner) MergeTree(ctx context.Context, base, head string) (string, error)` in `internal/gitcmd/gitcmd.go`
Call `r.runWithExitCode(ctx, "merge-tree", "--write-tree", base, head)`
Exit code 0: parse first line of stdout as tree SHA, return `(treeSHA, nil)`
Non-zero exit code: call `parseConflictFiles(stdout)` to extract conflicting paths, return `("", &MergeConflictError{ConflictingFiles: paths})`
Add godoc comment explaining that callers must use `errors.As` to extract `*MergeConflictError`
Note in comments that `merge-tree --write-tree` requires git >= 2.38 (enforced at construction)

subtasks.title: Implement RebaseAbort standalone method
details: Implement `func (r *GitRunner) RebaseAbort(ctx context.Context) error` in `internal/gitcmd/gitcmd.go`
Call `r.Run(ctx, "rebase", "--abort")` and return any error as-is
Add godoc comment explaining this is for edge-case manual recovery when context cancellation interrupts a rebase mid-flight
Note that `Rebase` calls this internally on conflict — `RebaseAbort` is only for the context-cancellation edge case

subtasks.title: Implement Rebase method with internal abort on conflict
details: Implement `func (r *GitRunner) Rebase(ctx context.Context, onto string) (string, error)` in `internal/gitcmd/gitcmd.go`
Call `r.runWithExitCode(ctx, "rebase", onto)`
On success (exit code 0): call `r.RevParse(ctx, "HEAD")` and return the new HEAD SHA

On non-zero exit (conflict): immediately call `r.Run(ctx, "rebase", "--abort")` to clean up rebase state, then parse conflicting files from stderr/stdout and return `("", &RebaseConflictError{ConflictingFiles: paths})`
Add godoc comment explaining the internal abort behavior and that callers must use `errors.As` to extract `*RebaseConflictError`
Document the distinction: conflict → `RebaseConflictError`; context cancellation → context error (caller must call `RebaseAbort` manually)

Parse git rebase conflict output to extract conflicting file paths — git rebase outputs `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in <path>` lines to stdout/stderr
Document the exact output format observed from git 2.38+ rebase in code comments alongside a representative sample
Reuse or adapt `parseConflictFiles` logic if the format is identical to merge-tree output
Return empty slice (not nil) if no conflict paths found
